title: The Run - Layered Roguelike Score with Stems - Dungeon Game Music Pack - 44 Tracks
tagline: 44 track roguelike score. 12 cues ship as four stacking stems: ground, drums, motion, theme. MIDI + OGG.
description:
The Run is a 44 track score for a roguelike or dungeon crawler, from the hub between runs to the way out: the title, the hub, the armoury, choosing a runner, the first door, 12 layered depths and skirmishes across four acts (the catacombs, the drowned works, the furnace and the heart), the peddler, the reliquary, the last lantern, an unmarked door, the hidden room, the cursed altar and the boss door, three act bosses, the final boss and a last stand, two elites, a training yard, a daily and an endless mode, the surface, the credits, and the cues a run fires all the time.

Twelve cues in four layers. The depths and the skirmishes ship twice: as the full mix, and as four stems that stack. L1 Ground is the harmony and the bass; L2 Drums is the taiko; L3 Motion is the motor figure and the counter line; L4 Theme is the lead, which states the cells. A game can play L1 alone on the first floor and add a stem as the run goes deeper or a fight starts, without changing tracks. The stems are the full mix split by part, note for note: every note of the cue is in exactly one stem. Each stem is the same length as the mix, carries the same LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH, and every layered cue loops from its first sample, so the stems stay aligned when they loop. 48 stems in all, as OGG and as MIDI. No other album in this studio's catalogue ships stems.

Checked, not promised. Every prefix of every stack (L1; L1 and L2; L1 to L3; all four) is run through the theory harness as an arrangement of its own: 384 of 384 checks pass, covering key, parallel fifths and octaves, register, range and no silent bar in the loop. That test found parallel fifths and octaves in the lower layers of 8 of the 12 cues, which the full mix hides because the lead is on top, and they were fixed before release. The stems are rendered at the full mix's own level: fitted back to the mix, every stem's best fit gain is within 0.06 dB of unity. Every added stem raises the loop level, the smallest step +0.58 dB. Tested in Godot 4.7.2: one cue's four stems load from the download and stack in the engine's AudioStreamSynchronized at the mix's length.

One theme, every track. Every one of the 44 tracks states Delve in its own shape, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI. 4 more themes sit beside it: one for the hub and the way home, one for the fights, one for what a run finds, and one for the bottom of the run and its bosses.

What is in it. 36 full pieces and 8 short cues, 41:07 of music in the full mixes, 10 in Aeolian, 10 in Dorian, 8 in Phrygian, 5 in Mixolydian, 5 in harmonic minor, 4 in Ionian and 2 in Lydian, 40 tracks in 4/4 and 4 in 3/4. A taiko drum plays in 24 tracks, never under a full piece's opening. Every note on the record is inside its track's declared mode. Between runs: The Run, Between Runs, The Armoury, Choose Your Runner, The First Door, The Training Yard, The Daily Descent, Endless and Again. The layered depths, three to an act: The Ossuary Stair, The Bone Galleries, Catacomb Skirmish, The Sluice Halls, The Pump Engines, Works Skirmish, The Slag Walks, The Bellows, Furnace Skirmish, The Root Vaults, The Pulse Below and Heart Skirmish. The rooms of a run: The Peddler, The Reliquary, The Last Lantern, An Unmarked Door, The Hidden Room, The Cursed Altar and The Boss Door. The fights: The Ossuary Warden, The Drowned Engineer, The Furnace King, The Heart of the Deep, The Run Ends Here, The Bonewright and The Ironclad. The way out: The Surface. Cues: Floor Cleared, Run Over, Stronger, A Relic, Unlocked, Cursed, A Moment of Rest and Boss Slain.

What you get. 44 OGG files, 36 of them with sample accurate LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags, which is what RPG Maker MV and MZ read. 44 editable .mid sources. 48 stem OGG files and their 48 stem .mid files. A Readme with per engine notes and how to layer the stems, the proof reports, and a royalty free commercial licence.

One family of 5 themes. Delve, Return, Blade, Hoard and Abyss. Delve falls two steps and springs back up a fourth: the run itself. Return climbs for the hub and the way home. Blade opens with a leap up a fifth for the fights. Hoard turns around a third for what a run finds. Abyss falls by thirds and ends a fifth lower than it began, for the bottom of the run. 1357 statements and fragments of those themes across the album, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI.

Gate results. 784 theory checks and 504 audio checks on the full mixes, 0 failed, plus the layer proof, and the reports ship inside the download. They say the music is correctly written, rendered, tagged and split. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks are for.

Three full tracks are free on this page, with their MIDI: The Run, the title theme, The Ossuary Stair, the first depth, with its four stems so you can try the layering in your own engine before you buy, and The Ossuary Warden, the first boss.

An honest note. The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont, so the taiko, brass, strings, choirs and synths are the General MIDI sounds of those names; load the MIDI into your own instruments to replace them. The dungeon and its acts are invented. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used anywhere.

devlog.title: The Run is out: a 44 track roguelike score, 12 cues in four stacking stems
devlog.body:
The Run is a 44 track score for a roguelike or dungeon crawler: the hub between runs, 12 layered depths and skirmishes across four acts, the rooms of a run (shop, treasure, rest, event, secret, curse, boss door), three act bosses, a final boss, two elites, a daily and an endless mode, and the cues a run fires all the time. It is live now, with three full tracks free to download from the page.

The idea. 12 of the cues ship as four stems that stack: Ground (the harmony and the bass), Drums (the taiko), Motion (the motor figure and the counter line), Theme (the lead, which states the cells). Play the first alone and add one as the run gets deeper or a fight starts. The stems are the full mix split by part, note for note, the same length and with the same loop tags, rendered at the mix's level. It is the first pack in our catalogue to ship stems.

How it was checked. Every prefix of every stack is checked as an arrangement of its own (384 of 384 checks pass); that is how parallel fifths and octaves hiding under the lead in 8 cues were found and fixed. Every stem's best fit gain against the mix is within 0.06 dB of unity, every added stem raises the loop level, and one cue's stems were loaded and stacked in Godot 4.7.2. Plus 784 theory checks and 504 audio checks on the full mixes, 0 failed, with the reports inside the download. Those numbers say the music is correctly written, rendered and split. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks (The Run, The Ossuary Stair and The Ossuary Warden) are for.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render; load the MIDI into your own instruments to replace the sounds. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used.
